source_doc: iHeart Offsite In Network Audience Extension_iAB Standard Tags

entities.name: Offsite In-Network Sponsorship
entities.description: A Q1 2026 product offering from Genuin that enables Commerce Media Teams to extend audio, programmatic, and social budgets across a network of publishers via iAB-compatible session takeover units.

entities.name: iAB Compatible Session Takeover
entities.description: An iAB-standard placement unit supporting 300x600 and 300x250 demo sizes that enables full-funnel activation across onsite and offsite contexts.

entities.name: Offsite Tag
entities.description: A tag created by Genuin for iHeart with 5 ad slots into which iHeart routes their demand for offsite in-network campaigns.

entities.name: Monetized Infrastructure
entities.description: Genuin's revenue model in which publishers pay for monetized infrastructure, while advertisers pay zero infrastructure fees and all media spend passes through transparently to network partners.

entities.name: Pay Genuin Direct
entities.description: Activation path where the marketer pays Genuin directly for all campaigns; Genuin generates the invoice and resolves payouts to all network publishers with full visibility.

entities.name: Pay Publisher Direct
entities.description: Activation path where the marketer leverages an existing direct relationship and payment setup with the publisher, requiring no new billing relationship with Genuin.

entities.name: Pay via RMN
entities.description: Activation path where the marketer pays their Retail Media Network, which then pays Genuin via a Genuin-generated invoice; Genuin resolves all publisher payouts.

entities.name: Retail Media Network
entities.description: Third-party retail media networks that marketers pay directly, which subsequently pay Genuin via Genuin-generated invoices in the RMN activation path.

entities.name: Full Funnel Measurement & Optimization
entities.description: Measurement capability that tracks out-of-market to in-market audience conversion with closed-loop attribution across every publisher placement.

entities.name: Zero-Party Data Ownership
entities.description: Data model where all engagement data (views, interactions, CTAs) belongs to the advertiser, sent back in raw format to their existing data infrastructure destinations.

entities.name: Reach, Frequency & Budget Optimization
entities.description: Capability to see activity on each publisher by payment path, reallocate budget in real time, and invite best-performing programmatic publishers directly into the network.

entities.name: Raw Data Shipback
entities.description: Process that returns all campaign data in raw format including publisher-level activity, spend, reach, frequency, engagement, and CTAs to the advertiser.

entities.name: MMP & Data Stack Mapping
entities.description: Integration step that connects campaign data to the advertiser's existing MMP, attribution partners, and analytics tools, pushing directly to their data warehouse.

entities.name: Certified Data Destinations
entities.description: Set of approved destinations (Google GCP, Amazon AWS, Oracle OCI, MixPanel, Snowflake, customer warehouse) to which Genuin delivers raw campaign data.

entities.name: Google GCP
entities.description: Google Cloud Platform listed as a certified data destination for Genuin campaign data.

entities.name: Amazon AWS
entities.description: Amazon Web Services listed as a certified data destination for Genuin campaign data.

entities.name: Oracle OCI
entities.description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure listed as a certified data destination for Genuin campaign data.

entities.name: MixPanel
entities.description: Analytics platform listed as a certified data destination for Genuin campaign data.

entities.name: Snowflake
entities.description: Cloud data warehouse listed as a certified data destination for Genuin campaign data.

entities.name: Data Processor Role
entities.description: Genuin's stated legal/operational posture in which it acts as a Data Processor rather than a Data Controller for advertiser engagement data.

entities.name: Network Tier Pricing
entities.description: Three-tier SOV pricing structure: T1 Test at $50k, T2 Launch at $500k, and T3 Scale at $5M for joining the network.

entities.name: iHeart
entities.description: Network partner publisher that routes ad demand through Genuin via Beeswax Ad Server and runs audience extension budgets at $1.70 CPM across the Genuin network of Infolink onsite properties.

entities.name: Grubhub
entities.description: Network partner publisher cited as an example destination for transparent advertiser pass-through media payments.

entities.name: Us Weekly
entities.description: Network partner publisher cited as an example destination for transparent advertiser pass-through media payments.

entities.name: Infolinks
entities.description: Partner that traffics the offsite tag across its 30K+ network of publishers with audio-on, providing dealIDs and fallback demand for iHeart campaigns.

entities.name: Beeswax Ad Server
entities.description: Ad server where iHeart connects multiple demand sources, performs ID sync with exchanges, and traffics VAST video and audio tags with fallback logic to Infolinks demand after 200 ms.

entities.name: Cookie Sync for Audience Extension
entities.description: Step 2 of the offsite in-network onboarding flow where iHeart provides ID sync to Infolinks so Beeswax buys and traffics only when ID mapping is established.

entities.name: VAST Tag
entities.description: Video and audio VAST tags created from Beeswax ad server by iHeart, with fallback logic to Infolinks demand if no ads render from the iHeart ad server within 200 ms.

entities.name: Audience Extension Buy
entities.description: iHeart-funded buy that runs audio and video ads at $1.70 CPM across the Genuin network of Infolinks onsite properties in iAB-compatible session takeover units.

entities.name: Trade Media Solution Subsidiary
entities.description: Genuin subsidiary that earns $0.10-$2 arbitrage margin by optimizing consumer experience curation, billed to Infolinks as a trade media solution and feed algorithm billing.

entities.name: JR LLC
entities.description: Partner LLC contracted with the Genuin subsidiary on a Year 1 30% / Year 2 20% / Year 3 10% revenue share, bringing other publishers and activating audience extension below $1 CPM to increase subsidiary margin.

entities.name: Commerce Media Teams
entities.description: Target audience for the Q1 2026 Offsite In-Network 'Getting Started' guide, focused on extending audio, programmatic, and social budgets.

entities.name: Marketers
entities.description: Buy-side audience that activates campaigns through one of the three payment paths (Pay Genuin Direct, Pay Publisher Direct, or Pay via RMN) and retains zero-party ownership of engagement data.

entities.name: Peter Bavaro
entities.description: US Partnership Sales contact at Genuin (peter@begenuin.com) named as the point of contact in the deck.

relationships.description: The Q1 2026 Getting Started guide for Offsite In-Network Sponsorship is aimed at Commerce Media Teams.
Offsite In-Network Sponsorship activates through iAB-compatible session takeover placement units.
Session takeover units support full-funnel activation and measurement.
Pay Genuin Direct is one of three activation/payment paths for Offsite In-Network Sponsorship.
Pay Publisher Direct is one of three activation/payment paths for Offsite In-Network Sponsorship.
Pay via RMN is one of three activation/payment paths for Offsite In-Network Sponsorship.
The Pay via RMN path depends on the marketer's Retail Media Network paying Genuin via invoice.
Monetized Infrastructure is the revenue model underpinning Offsite In-Network Sponsorship, with publishers paying Genuin in all activation paths.
Marketer dollars paid to Genuin pass through transparently to network partners including iHeart.
Marketer dollars paid to Genuin pass through transparently to network partners including Grubhub.
Marketer dollars paid to Genuin pass through transparently to network partners including Us Weekly.
Full-funnel measurement includes zero-party ownership of all engagement data by the advertiser.
Reach, frequency, and budget optimization is part of the full-funnel measurement offering.
Zero-party data ownership is delivered via raw data shipped back to the advertiser.
Raw data shipback is mapped against the advertiser's MMP and data stack as the next step.
MMP and data stack mapping pushes data into certified data destinations.
Google GCP is listed as a certified data destination.
Amazon AWS is listed as a certified data destination.
Oracle OCI is listed as a certified data destination.
MixPanel is listed as a certified data destination.
Snowflake is listed as a certified data destination.
Zero-party data ownership rests on Genuin acting as a Data Processor rather than a Data Controller.
Joining the Offsite In-Network Sponsorship network follows the T1/T2/T3 SOV pricing tiers.
Genuin creates the offsite tag with 5 ad slots specifically for iHeart to route their demand into.
Infolinks traffics the offsite tag across its 30K+ network of publishers with audio-on.
iHeart connects ad demand from multiple sources at Beeswax Ad Server and traffics campaigns from it.
iHeart provides ID sync to Infolinks as the second onboarding step for audience extension.
Beeswax performs ID sync with exchanges, only buying and trafficking when ID mapping is established.
iHeart creates video and audio VAST tags from Beeswax Ad Server for routing campaigns.
Fallback logic after 200 ms routes to Infolinks' existing demand if no iHeart ads render.
iHeart runs audience extension audio and video ads at $1.70 CPM in iAB-compatible session takeover units.
Audience extension budget runs across the Genuin network of Infolinks onsite properties with audio on.
iHeart funds the audience extension buy and gives Infolinks a $1.70 CPM IO for all offsite campaigns.
The Genuin subsidiary bills Infolinks as a trade media solution and feed algorithm billing arrangement, earning $0.10-$2 arbitrage margin.
The Genuin subsidiary has a revenue-share contract with JR LLC at Year 1 30%, Year 2 20%, and Year 3 10% of subsidiary revenue.
JR LLC brings other publishers and activates audience extension below $1 CPM to increase subsidiary margin.
Peter Bavaro, US Partnership Sales, is the named contact for the Offsite In-Network Sponsorship Q1 2026 program.
Marketers can activate by paying Genuin directly for all campaigns under this transparent pass-through path.
Marketers can activate using their existing direct relationship and payment setup with the publisher.
Marketers can pay their Retail Media Network, which then pays Genuin for campaign delivery.
